learningObjective: Reason about atomic contention: single-address hot-spot serialization vs block-local reduction + one atomic per block.

canonicalClaims.claim: Global atomics on a single hot address serialize at the atomic unit; canonical reductions perform block-local tree/warp reductions first and then issue at most one atomic per block, reducing contention by blockDim.
nonImplications: Does not imply atomics should never be used.
Does not imply SMEM tree reductions beat warp-shuffle reductions in the last stages.

misconceptions.claim: `atomicAdd` requires capturing the return value to commit the add.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The add is always committed; return is the old value, optional to use.

misconceptions.claim: Hardware atomic units have infinite bandwidth for FP32 atomicAdd on Ampere.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Contention on a single address serializes.

misconceptions.claim: SMEM tree reductions require `__syncwarp()` inside the loop beyond `__syncthreads()`.
misconceptions.whyWrong: `__syncthreads()` at block level is sufficient for this SMEM pattern.

misconceptions.claim: Contention is invisible at low N; atomicAdd cost is O(1) regardless.
misconceptions.whyWrong: At small N contention is low; scaling to large N reveals serialization.

implementationFacts: Hardware FP32 atomicAdd introduced with Pascal; FP64 later.
Best-practice reductions: warp-shuffle → SMEM → single atomic per block.
